title: ShaderMap 4 DDS export never writes a mip chain
content: Verified hands-on: ShaderMap 4 (v4.3.8, SM4 Pro Personal) can export DDS (tested DXT1, DXT3, and DXT5), via both the per-node "Save Map To File" dialog and the global Options -> Save Formats defaults, but it NEVER writes a mip chain into the file, regardless of which of those two export paths is used. This was confirmed by inspecting the DDS header of a freshly re-exported file: mipMapCount=1 and the DDSCAPS_MIPMAP flag is not set. There is no UI setting anywhere in ShaderMap 4 (checked both the per-node save dialog and the global Options -> Save Formats screen) to enable mip generation for DDS output -- the feature does not exist in this tool, it is not just an unchecked checkbox.

title: Materialize (PBR map generator) does not export DDS at all
content: Verified hands-on: Materialize (v1.78), a free alternative PBR-map generator, has no DDS export option at all. Its Saving Options only offer BMP, JPG, PNG, TGA, and TIFF. If Materialize is used to generate normal or specular maps for Fallout 4, the output must be exported as PNG or TGA and then converted/compressed to DDS with a separate tool (e.g. NVIDIA Texture Tools Exporter) -- Materialize cannot produce the final .dds itself.

title: Correct NVIDIA Texture Tools Exporter settings for FO4 normal/specular DDS with mipmaps
content: Working fix, verified hands-on, for producing a correct mipmapped DDS normal or specular map for Fallout 4 when the map was generated in ShaderMap 4 (which never writes mips, see texpipe-shadermap4-no-mipmaps) or Materialize (which cannot export DDS at all, see texpipe-materialize-no-dds): export the generated map from that tool as PNG or TGA, then import it into NVIDIA Texture Tools Exporter (2024.1.1). In NVIDIA Texture Tools Exporter: (1) leave "Generate Mipmaps" checked (it is checked by default) and use the Minimum/Maximum Mipmap Count controls, setting Maximum to MAX so the full chain is built down to 1x1. (2) For Format, choose plain "BC3 RGBA | 8bpp | DXT5: interpolated alpha" -- do NOT use "BC3n Normals" or "BC3n AGBR". Those are specialized channel-swap encodings meant only for shaders that specifically know to decode that layout, and will corrupt a normal map if the game/engine does not expect that exact encoding (Fallout 4's engine does not). (3) Leave "Image Type" set to "Color Map" when the input is an already-finished normal or specular map. The "Normal Map: Tangent Space" and "Normal Map: Object Space" Image Type options are NOT for correctly compressing an existing normal map -- confirmed via their in-app tooltips and the "Height Source" panel they reveal, they are generators that DERIVE a new normal map from a height/grayscale source image, and selecting either of them would corrupt an already-complete normal map instead of just compressing it. Context: Fallout 4 conventionally expects normal/specular maps as DXT5-compressed DDS with a full mip chain matching the diffuse texture's mip count (e.g. 12 levels for a 2048x2048 texture) -- a missing mip chain causes visibly incorrect texture behavior at a distance / under LOD transitions, even though the texture loads and looks fine up close.
